claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 52 COVID-19 patients and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls across Hong Kong and Atlanta showed increased plasmablast and effector CD8 T cell frequencies in infected individuals, prolonged effector CD8 T cell kinetics up to day 40 after symptom onset, reduced plasmacytoid dendritic cell frequencies, reduced pS6 in pDCs, decreased IκBα in myeloid dendritic cells, and reduced HLA-DR on monocytes and mDCs in severe COVID-19 versus healthy controls.

sources.quote: There was a notable increase in the frequency of plasmablast and effector CD8 T cells in all infected individuals ( Fig. 1B ) in both cohorts.
There were several differences, but notably the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was significantly reduced in the PBMCs of SARS-CoV-2–infected individuals in both cohorts ( Fig. 1C ).

We used mass cytometry to assess immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in 52 COVID-19 patients, who were confirmed positive for viral RNA by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls distributed between the two cohorts.

comparison.finding: increased plasmablast and effector CD8 T cell frequencies in infected individuals, reduced plasmacytoid dendritic cell frequencies, reduced pS6 in pDCs, decreased IκBα in myeloid dendritic cells, and reduced HLA-DR on monocytes and mDCs in severe COVID-19 versus healthy controls

claim_2.claim: Olink analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed significant up-regulation of 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, compared to healthy controls, with TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and oncostatin M correlating with clinical severity.

sources.section: Enhanced concentrations of cytokines and inflammatory mediators in plasma from COVID-19 patients
sources.quote: Of the 92 analytes measured, 71 proteins were detected within the dynamic range of the assay. Of these 71 proteins, 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 infection ( Fig. 3 , top row, and fig. S6).

sources.section: Enhanced concentrations of cytokines and inflammatory mediators in plasma from COVID-19 patients
sources.quote: In addition to IL-6 and other cytokines described previously ( 10 ), we identified three proteins that were significantly enhanced in COVID-19 infection and strongly correlated with clinical severity ( Fig. 3 , bottom row). These were TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and oncostatin M.

comparison.finding: significant up-regulation of 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10 in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls

claim_3.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from 7 COVID-19 patients and 5 healthy controls in the Atlanta cohort showed enhanced expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in COVID-19 patients, despite impaired type I IFN production by pDCs and myeloid cells.

sources.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
sources.quote: Notably, we detected clusters of T cells and monocytes that were characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, or ISG15 (see C11-C MONO_IFN and C18-T_IFN in fig. S10). These IFN response–enriched clusters emerged only in samples from COVID-19 patients (fig. S12).

sources.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
sources.quote: Notably, with the exception of modest levels of IFN-γ expression in T and NK cells, we could not detect any expression of IFN-α and -β genes, which is consistent with the functional data demonstrating impaired type I IFN production by pDCs and myeloid cells ( Fig. 2 ).

comparison.finding: enhanced expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in COVID-19 patients, despite impaired type I IFN production by pDCs and myeloid cells
